To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the soil organic matter (SOM) pool is a key target for agro-ecosystem restoration, that the SOM content is mainly controlled by SOM residence time and that the latter can be enhanced by considering the dynamics of nanoscale weathered minerals as a new key factor in SOM stabilization.
the soil organic matter (SOM) pool is a major target for agro-ecology.

(i) the soil organic matter (SOM) pool is the main target of agro-eco-logical strategies, (ii) SOM stabilization is governed by organomineral interactions at the nanoscale, and (iii), the current model of organo- mineral interactions in soils is too simplistic because it considers soil minerals as being stable and formed prior to SOM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interactions between organic compounds in soils and weathering mineral phases, which are key drivers of the residence time of soil organic carbon (OC).
the interactions of organic compounds and minerals in soils.
the fate of organic compounds in soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the soil organic matter (SOM) pool is the main target of agro- ecological strategies for three reasons (i) SOM plays key roles in the soil system functioning (nutrients, soil structure, microbial energy, and pollutant adsorbing), (ii) SOM represents the largest terrestrial carbon (C) stocks, and (iii), the intensification of agricultural practices has led to destabilization of significant quantities of SOM.
the current understanding of the organo-weathered mineralsorganic matter interface in soils has to be reconsidered.
the soil is the most important and most valuable resource of the biosphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the fate of organic matter (OM), and thus of the carbon stock, is governed by the dynamics of weathering minerals, which are the main components of soils and are the most important drivers of soil functioning.
the soil organic matter is a dynamic pool that is constantly changing in terms of quantity, quality and structure.
soil minerals are not stable surfaces but are subjected to dynamic weathering processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil OM pool should no longer be considered as the sum of the different OM fractions but as a continuum that results from a combination between OM and minerals.
we need to rethink the way we model soil organic matter stabilization and that we should not consider soil minerals as stable.

the fate of organic compounds in soil is not solely controlled by the chemical composition of the organic molecules, but also by the mineral phases with which they come into contact, and by the dynamics of the mineral phases.
